minimumCases.rationale: Dataset v3 has 90 cases. A smoke run (5 cases) must never produce a PASS, and a partial run must not either: the gate decides on the full dataset only. Starting value, to be raised if the dataset grows.

deterministicChecks.rationale: Schema, completeness, uniqueness, and dataset integrity are not statistical. A single failure means the evidence is unusable, so the requirement is 100 percent.

criticalErrors.rationale: With 90 cases, zero critical cases gives a one-sided 95 percent Clopper-Pearson upper bound of 3.3 percent and one critical case gives 5.2 percent. A 3.5 percent limit is therefore zero tolerance at this sample size, the tightest limit 90 cases can demonstrate. Severity rules v2 add wrong_value, so a wrong amount or identifier in an answer now counts. Starting value pending the first live v3 run.

zeroWidthInterval.rationale: When the arms agree on every repeat of every case, the percentile bootstrap interval collapses to a point and clears any margin. That shows no observed regression, not proven non-inferiority: 90 identical cases still allow up to 3.3 percent of cases to differ. The gate passes with an explicit warning. Kept from thresholds-v1; revisit after the first live v3 run shows how often the arms disagree.

nonInferiority.rationale: Kept at the 3 point margin of thresholds-v1. At 90 cases and 80 percent power the minimum detectable paired difference is about 9 points at 10 percent discordance and 13 points at 20 percent (src/stats/power.ts), so a 3 point margin is confirmable only when the arms almost never disagree. Expect INCONCLUSIVE for small real differences; that is the correct output.
Kept at 3 points. Declared extra reads no longer fail tool accuracy in v3, so the metric measures plan adherence rather than penalising reasonable verification calls.
Kept at 3 points. Recovery applies to 18 cases in v3 (8 in v2), so it is decidable more often, but expect INCONCLUSIVE whenever several recovery cases differ between arms.
